messages:
kevin: Heads up — nightly perf run shows a p95 regression on the paged-attn path for long-context streaming workloads. baseline ~45ms, current p95 ~120ms with 4 concurrent streams. noticed around 03:10 UTC.

ci-bot: nightly/perf/paged-attn (models: rw-7b) failed perf-threshold check (p95 increased). job: https://ci/jobs/1862345680 :rotating_light:

tara: I started a quick nvprof + CUPTI capture. early signal: a lot more time spent in a fallback kernel (fused_matmul_slow) instead of FlashAttn_v2 for these runs. fallback rate ~27%.

kevin: any idea what triggers the fallback? model variant, seq len, or fragmentation?

tara: digging — the block-table allocator is producing more small, non-contiguous kv pages under concurrent writes, which increases page-walks during attention. FlashAttn_v2 requires contiguous page blocks for the fused kernel path; when fragmentation > ~30% selection logic opts for the safe fused_matmul path.

srinivas: Interesting. The heuristic in kernel_selector.cpp is currently:
```
if (contiguity_score >= 0.7 && seq_len >= 64) use FlashAttn_v2;
else use fused_matmul;
```
We compute contiguity_score from block_table.backed_pages / logical_pages. Fragmentation makes that metric noisy under concurrent frees.

dana: Could also be allocator churn — many ephemeral allocations for attention windows cause block-table churn and more small descriptors. We saw similar with the embedding cache. My local trace shows:
```
alloc() small 128B x 10k
free() interleaved
block_table.gaps++
page_walks++
```
If we defer reclamation (grace period) or use page-aligned pooling we could reduce noisy gaps.

kevin: Can we get a profile snippet (GPU timeline + scheduler events)?

tara: pasted a tiny excerpt from the CUPTI timeline (trimmed):
```
[03:09:58] FlashAttn_v2 kernel  GPU:  3.2ms (20%)
[03:09:58] fused_matmul_slow GPU: 12.1ms (72%)  <-- jumped
[03:09:59] page_walk_kernel      GPU:  2.8ms (8%)
```
and a host-side trace: many concurrent block_table.update() calls and small memcpy ops.

olgav: We should add telemetry for: `block_table_fill_rate`, `page_walks_per_token`, and `kernel_fallback_rate` per model+route. That will let us correlate more easily.

srinivas: For immediate mitigation I propose a two-pronged approach: 1) allocator change to a hybrid pool that hands out whole-page-aligned KV slabs for heavy-attn routes; 2) tweak kernel_selector to include a hysteresis window so small transient fragmentation doesn't force fallback.

kevin: Concrete proposals?

srinivas: Patch sketch:
```
// hybrid allocator
if (request_route == "attn_stream") {
  if (size >= SLAB_THRESHOLD) return page_pool.alloc_pages(n_pages);
  else return freelist_small.alloc(size);
}
```
plus a compaction job that runs every N allocations to coalesce adjacent free pages.

tara: I prototyped a kernel_selector tweak: keep last_good_contiguity for 500ms and require two consecutive samples < threshold before switching to safe kernel. Seems to reduce noisy fallbacks in my local repro.

dana: Another option: optimistic launch of FlashAttn_v2 with a fallback kernel queued — if FlashAttn fails because pages not contiguous, fallback runs. But that risks wasting GPU cycles. Might be ok for low-qps test jobs but not production.

kevin: I like hysteresis + allocator change as low-risk. Dana help with compaction heuristics and metrics. Tara can push the kernel_selector patch and rerun nightly. Olgav add the telemetry metrics. Srinivas please prototype page-aligned pool.

olgav: I'll add dashboards: heatmap of `page_walks_per_token` vs `p95_latency`, and alerts if `kernel_fallback_rate` > 10% for 5m.

ci-bot: Perf job created: nightly/perf/paged-attn-repro-1862345701. See logs when finished.

kevin: Thanks — action items noted. We'll regroup after the next perf run. :thumbsup:

tara: one more note — the fused attention microbenchmarks still show FlashAttn_v2 wins for seq_len <= 256 when contiguous; so preserving contiguity is high ROI.

dana: ack. starting compaction experiment locally now. will post perf diffs.

srinivas: I'll try a synthetic that floods small allocations to stress the block table and measure the break-even for the pool approach.

kevin: Great. If anyone hits a clear regression repro, paste the minimal repro here and we can prioritize a rollback if needed.

[thread closed after coordination and CI kick-off]
